title: Successive root nerves, adjunction normalization and puncture-map naturality
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Fix a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; put $C_{F,T}=p_T^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories and direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-regular-scheme], let $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ be a reduced strict normal crossings divisor with finitely many components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and put $W=Y\setminus D$. Let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Assume that on every strict henselization at a geometric point, with parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ cutting out the branches of $D$, $L$ becomes constant on the inverse-limit cover of the complement obtained by adjoining compatible $n$th roots of all $t_i$ for every $n$ prime to $p$. This is the meaning of tame here; with no branches the cover is the identity. This is strict-local Kummer tameness [def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module]. Write $L_F=C_{F,W}\otimes_{C_{E,W}}L$, an ordinary tensor, for $F=E,\Omega$.
Let $L'$ satisfy the same lisse and strict-local Kummer-tame hypotheses as $L$, and let $f:L\to L'$ be an actual $C_{E,W}$-module morphism. For $J\subseteq A$, partitioned as $J=J_o\sqcup J_i$ with $J_i\ne\varnothing$, put $S_J=(\bigcap_{d\in J}D_d)\setminus\bigcup_{d\notin J}D_d$ with reduced structure and inclusion $s_J:S_J\to Y$. There are affine etale charts $B_\alpha\to Y\setminus\bigcup_{d\notin J}D_d$ with equations $t_d$ for $d\in J$, affine pro-etale $U_\alpha\to B_\alpha$, and a pro-etale covering $v_\alpha:T_\alpha=U_\alpha\times_Y S_J\to S_J$, together with compatible roots of unity. Let
$$\mathcal T_\alpha=\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}_{U_\alpha}(\mathcal O_{U_\alpha}[x_d]_{d\in J}/(x_d^n-t_d)_d),\qquad \mathcal T_\alpha^\circ=\mathcal T_\alpha\times_YW,$$
with power transitions. There is a deck-equivariant lisse extension $\mathcal N_\alpha$ of the actual pullback of $L$ to $\mathcal T_\alpha$, with boundary module $p_{T_\alpha}^*M_{\alpha,E}$ for a finite-dimensional continuous $E$-representation $M_\alpha$ of $G_J=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^J$. Here $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_m\mathbf Z/q^m\mathbf Z$. Its ordinary extension to $C_\Omega$ is lisse, restricts to the actual pullback of $L_\Omega$, and has boundary $p_{T_\alpha}^*M_{\alpha,\Omega}$, so the charts, roots and cover are simultaneous for both fields. Through the chosen roots of unity, $\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ\to U_\alpha\times_YW$ is a pro-etale covering and a $G_J$-torsor for the root deck action.

The family can be chosen simultaneously for $L,L'$ with equivariant extensions $\mathcal N_\alpha,\mathcal N'_\alpha$, boundary representations $M_\alpha,M'_\alpha$, and maps $\widetilde f_\alpha:\mathcal N_\alpha\to\mathcal N'_\alpha$ restricting to the actual pullback of $f$. Each $\widetilde f_\alpha$ is the unique extension of this puncture map. It commutes with the action for every continuous profinite family of deck transformations. Its boundary map is $p_{T_\alpha}^*$ of a continuous $E$-linear $G_J$-equivariant map $m_\alpha:M_\alpha\to M'_\alpha$; for $\Omega$ the map is its ordinary scalar extension. On every further common refinement of such families these assertions hold for the actual restricted maps, and two supplied extensions of the same puncture module are uniquely isomorphic by an isomorphism restricting to the identity.
Write $G_o=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^{J_o}$ and $G_i=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^{J_i}$, so $G_J=G_o\times G_i$ by coordinate reordering. On $U_\alpha\times_YW$, let $\mathcal T_{\alpha,i}^\circ$ and $\mathcal T_{\alpha,o}^\circ$ be the towers with only inner and only outer root equations, respectively. Adjoining inner roots and then outer roots is canonically equivariantly isomorphic to $\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ$, with commuting actions. Their successive augmented nerves, inner first and outer second, have parameters $G_o^a\times G_i^b$; the diagonal is the full root nerve with parameters $(G_o\times G_i)^n$.
For either boundary representation $M$ on this chart and $F=E,\Omega$, let
$$B_F^{a,b}(M)=R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[G_o^a\times G_i^b],M_F),\qquad M_F(P)=C(P,F\otimes_E M).$$
Here $F\otimes_E M$ has the product norm topology, $C_F[P]$ is the free internal module on $Q\mapsto C(Q,P)$, and internal Hom is right adjoint to module tensor, derived in its second variable. Actions, inflation adjunctions and derived invariants are those of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data]; derived categories are ordinary unbounded K-injective ones [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use coherent nonnegative resolutions, with total differential $d_o+(-1)^a d_i+(-1)^{a+b}d_{\rm res}$. The successive geometric augmentations give a natural derived isomorphism
$$\gamma_F:p_{T_\alpha}^*\operatorname{Tot}_{\Delta}B_F^{\bullet,\bullet}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}p_{T_\alpha}^*R\Gamma_{G_o}(R\Gamma_{G_i}^{G_o}(M_F[0])).$$
Its composite with the full-bar identification $p_{T_\alpha}^*R\Gamma_{G_o\times G_i}(M_F[0])\cong p_{T_\alpha}^*\operatorname{Tot}_{\Delta}B_F^{\bullet,\bullet}(M)$ is $p_{T_\alpha}^*\theta_{M_F}$, where $\theta$ is the ordinary K-injective derived comparison conjugate to composition of the specified exact inflations, induced by $M_F^{G_o\times G_i}=(M_F^{G_i})^{G_o}$. Its units and counits are those of the composite adjunction. These object and arrow comparisons commute with $m_{\alpha,F}$ and the actual maps induced by $f$ on both geometric nerves, and restrict under common refinements of charts. All assertions are in the derived category, including the augmentation arrow. They hold for both fields on the same charts without interchanging scalar extension with a direct image. They include empty strata, trivial outer group and rank zero. Sites are small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; continuous representations and their condensed actions use [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data, def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and all derived categories are the ordinary ones [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-snc-universal-residual-charts] with $I=J$. Use its connected affine residual charts $B_\alpha,U_\alpha,T_\alpha$ and connected full and punctured towers $\mathcal T_\alpha,\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ$, including compatible roots. Its strict-local connectedness and qcqs assertions supply the tower hypothesis of [lem-sfb-tame-integral-reduction-family]. Apply that statement separately to $L,L'$: obtain integral lattices, their actual finite quotient systems and their constant restrictions on each punctured strict-local root tower. The charts depend on the pair geometry, so the same charts serve both systems.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: On each chosen chart apply [lem-sfb-snc-tame-finite-fibre-classification] to the two finite quotient systems. Its naturality and finite-product clauses give finite module fibres, their quotient maps and their actual root-deck descent actions, compatible with all reductions. Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-adic-fibre-realization] separately to these systems, with $B=U_\alpha\times_YW$ and $X=\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ$. Obtain finite-dimensional continuous representations $M_\alpha,M'_\alpha$ and equivariant isomorphisms of their pulled-back continuous-function modules with the actual pullbacks of $L,L'$. Both use the same full root tower, not successive choices of towers for separate finite levels.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: Define $\mathcal N_\alpha=p_{\mathcal T_\alpha}^*C(-,M_\alpha)$ and likewise $\mathcal N'_\alpha$. Give them the action combining root rotation with the representation on their fibres. A finite $E$-basis makes each module $C_{E,\mathcal T_\alpha}^d$, hence lisse. The isomorphisms in step 2 specify their puncture identifications. Setting roots to zero and composing point pullbacks gives their stated boundary identifications. Ordinary extension to $C_\Omega$ sends that finite basis to $C_{\Omega,\mathcal T_\alpha}^d$; it therefore has boundary $p_{T_\alpha}^*C(-,\Omega\otimes_E M_\alpha)$ and the actual puncture restriction. The finite product norm is precisely the one used in these identifications.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: Restrict the actual pullback of $f$ through the puncture identifications of step 2. By [lem-sfb-root-tower-lisse-morphism-extension] it extends uniquely to $\widetilde f_\alpha:\mathcal N_\alpha\to\mathcal N'_\alpha$. In finite bases its entries are global sections of $C_{E,\mathcal T_\alpha}$. The continuous-function realization [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] identifies them with continuous functions $|\mathcal T_\alpha|\to E$. Since $\mathcal T_\alpha$ is nonempty connected by step 1 and $E$ is totally disconnected, every such function is constant: the image of a connected space is connected, and connected subsets of $E$ are singletons. Thus the whole extension is a matrix over $E$, defining $m_\alpha:M_\alpha\to M'_\alpha$. Finite matrices over a normed field are continuous. Its boundary map is exactly $p_{T_\alpha}^*m_\alpha$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: For a profinite family $g:Q\to G_J$, compare the two composites expressing equivariance on $\mathcal T_\alpha[Q]$. Their puncture restrictions are equal because $f$ is a map downstairs and the supplied actions are actual descent actions. By [lem-sfb-root-tower-profinite-base-change], this is a full root tower over the affine pro-etale chart $U_\alpha[Q]$. Apply the injectivity in [lem-sfb-root-tower-lisse-morphism-extension] there: the composites agree on the whole $Q$-parametrized object. On the boundary this says $m_\alpha\rho(g)=\rho'(g)m_\alpha$; in particular $m_\alpha$ is $G_J$-equivariant. This proves family equivariance, rather than checking only individual deck elements.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: The chart construction admits common pointed refinements by [lem-sfb-snc-universal-residual-charts], and the finite-fibre and adic-realization comparisons of step 2 restrict along these refinements. The morphism-extension bijection commutes with pro-etale base change, so the restricted $\widetilde f_\alpha$ is the unique extension of the restricted puncture map. More generally for two supplied lisse extensions, extend the identity on their common puncture and its inverse by that bijection; their composites restrict to identities and hence are identities. For either field this uniqueness also follows directly from [lem-sfb-root-tower-puncture-invariance]: applying $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal N,-)$ to $\mathcal N'\simeq Rj_*j^*\mathcal N'$ and the derived adjunction gives the same restriction bijection in degree zero. Thus uniqueness and identity-restricting comparison isomorphisms hold on further common refinements, including for the ordinary $\Omega$-extensions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: At finite root orders $n_i,n_o$, adjoining roots of the two disjoint parameter lists in succession has algebra $R[x_d\ (d\in J_i),y_d\ (d\in J_o)]/(x_d^{n_i}-t_d,y_d^{n_o}-t_d)$, independent of the order. The coordinate maps fix $R$ and each named root. They commute with all power transitions and with rotations in either list. Passing to the full towers gives the required canonical equivariant isomorphism: diagonal orders are cofinal among pairs, since any pair divides its least common multiple, which is still prime to $p$. The two rotations commute because they change disjoint coordinates. Apply [lem-sfb-compatible-kummer-tower-cech] to each list and to their union to identify the torsor fibre products and all transitions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: Use the torsor coordinates $(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx)$ of [lem-sfb-compatible-kummer-tower-cech]. The successive action nerves have term $\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ[G_o^a\times G_i^b]$: in one direction multiply adjacent outer labels or omit an endpoint, and in the other do the same to inner labels. Degeneracies insert the identity; moving the base vertex acts on the coefficient. The two directions commute by step 7 and by commutation of the two coefficient actions. On the diagonal, $(g_1,\ldots,g_n;h_1,\ldots,h_n)\mapsto((g_1,h_1),\ldots,(g_n,h_n))$ identifies every face, degeneracy and augmentation with the full product-group nerve. This also fixes the order: inner invariants first, retaining the outer action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: For every $a,b$ apply [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity] with profinite parameter $P=G_o^a\times G_i^b$ to either supplied extension from step 3. It identifies the boundary restriction of that geometric nerve term with $p_{T_\alpha}^*B_F^{a,b}(M)$. Naturality in $P$ identifies multiplication, deletion and identity-insertion operators. Its compatibility with profinite families of automorphisms identifies the action first face on the entire parameter object. Hence these are coherent bicosimplicial comparisons, including the augmentations, not merely independent identifications of terms. Use [lem-sfb-derived-cech-image-totalization] for the two coverings to retain the augmented compatible first-quadrant resolution models and their actual restriction-of-sections arrows.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-product-bar-comparison] with $A=C_F$, $G=G_o$, $H=G_i$ and $N=M_F$. Its diagonal identifies with the full root nerve of step 8 and its iterated bar with the successive geometric augmentations of step 9. Thus its natural diagonal-to-iterated isomorphism, followed by its iterated-invariants identification, gives $\gamma_F$. Its stated arrow normalization says that the composite with the full-bar identification is exactly $p_{T_\alpha}^*\theta_{M_F}$. The resolution differential has the required signs $d_o+(-1)^ad_i+(-1)^{a+b}d_{\rm res}$; finite nonnegative diagonals allow the exact $p_{T_\alpha}^*$ to be applied termwise, as in the Cech-totalization statement. No underived continuous-function complex replaces any derived internal Hom.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: For the normalization of adjunctions, use the specified exact inflations of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. Inflation to the product action is their composite and its conjugate on right adjoints is $N^{G_o\times G_i}=(N^{G_i})^{G_o}$. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] to those exact left adjoints and the identity composite identification. It states that the ordinary K-injective comparison is precisely the derived conjugate and that its unit and counit are the composite unit and counit. Together with the comparison-arrow assertion in step 10 this gives the requested adjunction normalization of $\gamma_F$, not an arbitrary isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: In each $(a,b)$ term the coefficient map is postcomposition by $m_{\alpha,F}$ in $R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C_F[G_o^a\times G_i^b],-)$. It commutes with the first faces because $m_{\alpha,F}\rho(g)=\rho'(g)m_{\alpha,F}$, and with interior faces and degeneracies because these precompose on the parameter. Naturality of the boundary-acyclicity comparison identifies that map with the actual geometric map induced by $f$. Naturality of augmented Cech totalization and of the product-bar comparison therefore gives the commutative square $\gamma_{F,M'}\circ\operatorname{Tot}_\Delta B_F(m)=R\Gamma_{G_o}(R\Gamma_{G_i}^{G_o}(m))\circ\gamma_{F,M}$ after point pullback. Every augmentation square is included because each cited comparison retains its specified augmentation. Their stated pro-etale base-change naturality gives the identical square after any common chart refinement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: For $\Omega$ use the ordinary scalar extensions of the finite free extensions and of $\widetilde f_\alpha$. In the finite bases of step 4 the matrix is $1\otimes m_\alpha$, so the boundary map is the ordinary scalar extension of $m_\alpha$. Uniqueness from step 6 identifies it with the actual extended puncture map. Repeat steps 9--12 for this supplied $\Omega$-extension: boundary acyclicity explicitly covers both fields and their common root data, and the formal product-bar theorem applies to either condensed coefficient ring. Thus both fields satisfy the assertions on the same charts. This argument applies the two direct-image calculations separately; no interchange of scalar tensor with direct image enters it.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive Kummer nerves and puncture-map naturality

proof.text: For an empty stratum choose the empty covering family. For rank zero all representations, maps and comparison objects are zero. If $J_o=\varnothing$, the outer tower is the identity, the outer group is trivial, and its unnormalized nerve has only identity parameters and identity operators; the product-bar theorem explicitly includes this case with the specified augmentations. The remaining inner group and the same finite-diagonal totalization give all asserted arrows. These conventions are compatible with restrictions and uniqueness in the preceding steps.
